ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the shaded area in the figure is located near about 35°N and close to the 110°E meridian; the Yellow River and provincial boundaries can be seen on the right side. The figure also has contour lines of 500 meters and 1000 meters, showing that the shaded area is near the Yellow River and in a region related to the Loess Plateau. Then reason: the stem calls this area the “dry belt,” indicating that drought is its significant characteristic; but from its location, this region is still affected by the monsoon climate. In a monsoon climate, precipitation has large seasonal and interannual variation, and unstable precipitation easily occurs, thereby leading to frequent droughts and floods. Therefore, in terms of climatic disasters, another main natural factor restricting agricultural development in this region is frequent drought and flood disasters caused by the monsoon climate.
